custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use two Part Library entries from before this release that have exactly the same part number, with the same upper and lower case, and different descriptions (such pairs come only from data saved before this release); call that part number number 1.
    • How to do it: Click Parts in the top bar, then Part Library in the left menu, click Search and type a part number; a pair shows as two rows with the same Part Number and different Description.
  • Make sure no part at the test location has a part number that matches number 1, ignoring upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces.
  • Use a description for the new part, description 3, that neither entry has.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Inventory Part window opens.

Step 2:

  • Description reads description 3.

Step 3:

  • Part Number reads number 1.

Step 4:

  • The category shows in the Category field.

Step 5:

  • Cost reads $10.00.

Step 6:

  • The window closes and the part is saved.
  • No message about the Part Library appears (no "Linked to" message).

Step 7:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 8:

  • Three entries now have number 1: the two old entries with their own descriptions, unchanged, and a new one with description 3 (2 + 1 = 3).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S7-R8: “If more than one entry matches, the system creates a Part Library entry of its own for the new part.”
  • S7-R10: “No message about the Part Library is shown when the descriptions match, or when a new entry is created.”
  • Story 7, context note: “Context note: S7-R4 to S7-R8 decide which Part Library entry a new part shares. Linking happens only on an exact match. A number that matches several entries exactly, or none, never gets guessed onto one of them.”
